# API coverage

<!-- Generated by bin/php/tron-inventory.php; do not edit by hand. Regenerate it after a change to modules, fetch functions,
     operators, settings, scripts or the adapters. -->

Every API point of the installation this catalog was made on, found in its files (never listed by hand), with its risk class and
whether tron covers it, and by which tool. Generated 2026-11-25T06:14:02Z by `bin/php/tron-inventory.php`; the same data as JSON is
`doc/api-coverage.json`, and the tools `system_catalog` and `system_coverage` answer from it.

## How to read it

- **Point**: one thing code, templates, scripts or an agent can call: a module view, a fetch function, an operator, a script ...
- **Risk class**: `read` reads only; `write` changes content an editor owns; `admin` changes the system or other people's rights;
  `dangerous` removes or replaces what cannot simply be made again. From the point's own declaration where it has one (a fetch
  function's `operation_types`, a command's "dry run unless --apply"), else from the words of its name, read conservatively: an
  unknown word counts as a write (fetch functions and operators excepted, which read by nature).
- **Covered**: a tool runs it today, as the calling Exponential user, permission-checked, redacted and audited. A read point is
  covered when a tool executes it; a write, admin or dangerous point only when a tool runs it as a dry run (its dry-run twin). The
  `by` column names the tool; `unit` marks a unit of the units programs, `adapter` a generic adapter of the program `system`.
- **Planned**: for a point not covered, the unit or step that will cover it. Writes stay inactive until their dry-run twin exists.
- Every point is described by `system_catalog` whether covered or not; describing is not counted as covering.
- The INI blocks are many and all read; the totals per area below show the coverage without them too.

## Regenerating

From the installation root, on a node where a heavy job is allowed:

```bash
php extension/tron/bin/php/tron-inventory.php --siteaccess=<sa>                        # the summary
php extension/tron/bin/php/tron-inventory.php --siteaccess=<sa> --write                # var/tron/api-coverage.json (the tools read it)
php extension/tron/bin/php/tron-inventory.php --siteaccess=<sa> --doc=extension/tron/doc   # this page and its JSON
php extension/tron/bin/php/tron-inventory.php --siteaccess=<sa> --area=module_view --uncovered
```

It reads module.php, function_definition.php and operation_definition.php of every module, the template operator
autoloads, the merged content.ini, workflow.ini, cronjob.ini and expqueue.ini of the siteaccess, the INI files, the
autoload arrays (service classes) and `bin/php/console list`. It writes only where asked. The JSON has one point per
line, so a regenerated catalog diffs point by point.

## Left out

Only active extensions count. What the installation names in `[SystemAdapterSettings] PrivateNames[]` (set in
`settings/override`; its other MCP servers, private client projects ...) is left out of the catalog and of the system
tools, so those names appear nowhere in it.
